newsitem.title: UK: London gold quiet, but tone of market bearish.
newsitem.headline: London gold quiet, but tone of market bearish.

text.p: Gold prices were slightly lower early on Thursday after a half-hearted stab to the upside was turned back by Asian selling.
Prices were seen stuck in a tight range for the time being, although market sentiment was increasingly bearish and gold remained vulnerable to the downside, dealers added.
Bullion fixed at $378.50 an ounce, compared to $379.10 on Wednesday afternoon and a London close of $378.90/$379.40.

"The gold price is very disappointing. It wasn't able to break above $380 yesterday, even though normally this is a strong time of year for gold and given the relative strenth of silver," a London-based dealer said.
"If $380 is so difficult for gold then I wouldn't be surprised to see a test of $377," he added.
Gold had ticked higher on Wednesday afternoon after news of a wider than expected U.S. trade deficit depressed the dollar.
But it stopped short of the psychological $380 an ounce resistance level, and selling in Asia and Australia pushed prices lower overnight.
Early European trading was uneventful, although some light buying emerged to hold gold above its critical support level around $377 an ounce, dealers said.
Technical analysts said historical price charts suggested that a breach of that level could send gold spiralling down to fresh 19-month lows.

But the expiry next week of over-the-counter options, which give holders the right but not the obligation to buy or sell gold at a give prices, could help gold edge slightly higher in the meantime, dealers said.
Silver was stronger than gold, analysts said, but it, too, came off highs on Wednesday before reaching the critical resistance level of $5.00 an ounce.
It was indicated at $4.93/$4.95 an ounce, down two cents from Wednesday's London close. Platinum was expected to remain very quiet in a tight $383-$385 range, dealers said.
It was indicated virtually unchanged from Wednesday's London close at $384.00/$385.00 an ounce.
Its sister metal palladium was also little changed at $117.50/$118.50 an ounce, down $0.50.
